items.title: What’s next: Key climate and nature standards in 2026
items.summary: Welcome to the Trellis timeline of updates and public consultations regarding voluntary net zero, carbon accounting, nature and circular economy standards — both established guidance and emerging frameworks.

items.title: Sustainability leadership moves
items.summary: As corporate sustainability matures, some long-time leaders are leaving the profession, while others are tackling a broader set of responsibilities following reorganizations or layoffs.

items.title: COP17 mobilises $1.3bn for land restoration and drought resilience
items.summary: Kicking off week two of the conference, governments, development banks, funds and businesses have announced over $1bn in new and pipeline finance to tackle desertification, with a focus on restoring rangelands.

items.title: Could Norway’s oil and gas plans pave the way for more UK fossil fuel projects?
items.summary: As the UK ponders future oil and gas sites in the North Sea, the Norwegian Government is challenging the courts over ‘invalid’ fossil fuel projects, stating it would continue expansion activities in the Arctic regardless of EU bans.

items.title: Weakened ZEV Mandate would cut £1.5bn from EV charging sales
items.summary: Weakening the Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Mandate could reduce flexible charging capacity by 12GW over the next eight years, at a cost of £1.56bn in sales, new research has found.

items.title: Why every business just got a stake in the High Seas
items.summary: The UK’s ratification of the High Seas Treaty is a major step towards stronger ocean protection.

items.title: THREE WEEKS to go until edie’s Sustainable Supply Chains Summit
items.summary: Join us on 17 September for a unique opportunity to gain expert-led insights through thought leadership and industry panels featuring top professionals in sustainability, supply chain and procurement.
